commands.command: cargo new / edit: repopact-provider-github/src/{headers.rs,rest.rs}; extend transport.rs with ReqwestTransport/RestTransport; extend device_flow.rs with refresh_access_token; add repopact-remote-provider/src/credential_os.rs; add keyring + reqwest to rust/Cargo.toml workspace.dependencies
commands.summary: Real production HTTP transport: reqwest blocking client, rustls-tls (no OpenSSL/native-tls Android cross-compilation burden), redirect::Policy::none() with a hand-rolled redirect loop enforcing Decision 0061's Authorization-header allowlist, explicit connect (10s)/overall (30s) timeouts, and a bounded (8MB) streamed read via Read::take rather than trusting Content-Length. Centralized headers (headers.rs): Accept, X-GitHub-Api-Version, User-Agent (GitHub rejects requests with no User-Agent), Authorization built once per request. Real OS-protected credential store: keyring crate (windows-native/apple-native/sync-secret-service backends), OsCredentialStore implementing put/get/delete against the real Windows Credential Manager on this machine; Android has no backend here and is not silently faked (see Android disposition below).

authorization_survives_redirect_only_to_an_allowlisted_host (pure policy-decision unit test) and a_real_redirect_to_a_non_allowlisted_host_does_not_carry_the_authorization_header (a genuine integration test: two real local TCP servers, a real HTTP 302 redirect from one to the other, the second server's actually-received request headers inspected on the wire) both pass. The Authorization header is provably absent at the second hop -- not merely asserted never sent by mock bookkeeping.

commands.summary: 4/4 live tests passed against real api.github.com, no client ID/auth needed: live_resolves_a_real_public_branch_to_its_commit_sha (octocat/Hello-World heads/master -> 40-char hex SHA); live_peels_a_real_annotated_tag_on_a_well_known_public_repository (torvalds/linux tags/v6.1, a real GPG-signed annotated kernel-release tag -- proves the object.type=="tag" peel path against live data, not only a scripted fixture); live_canonicalizes_a_short_sha_on_a_real_public_repository (7fd1a60 -> the full documented 40-char SHA); live_lists_branches_on_a_real_public_repository. This is real, live proof of GH-006's ref-resolution/immutable-revision requirement independent of the operator's GitHub App registration gate.

5 non-ignored tests pass against the real Windows Credential Manager (put/get round-trip, delete, missing-entry-is-None, overwrite, distinct-kinds-do-not-collide). Discovered and fixed a real flakiness: Windows Credential Manager occasionally returns a transient error on a delete issued immediately after a put/overwrite in the same process; CleanupGuard now retries up to 5 times with a 50ms backoff and panics loudly (rather than silently leaving a real OS entry behind) if all retries fail. Verified reliable across 3 consecutive full runs with zero stray entries confirmed via `cmdkey /list` after each.

commands.summary: The strongest available automated proof of GH-004 restart persistence in this non-interactive session (standing in for a manual close-Workbench/reopen-Workbench cycle): process A wrote a real access-token-shaped credential to the real Windows Credential Manager and exited; a separate OS process (`cmdkey /list`) independently confirmed the entry existed with the expected target name; process C (a fresh cargo test invocation) read the value back correctly with no shared in-memory state; process D deleted it; a final `cmdkey /list` confirmed zero remaining RepoPact entries. Credential persistence and deletion are proven at the real OS level, not merely within one process's lifetime.
